pain.headline: You are still the bottleneck between your brief and the result.
pain.paragraph: Founders and operators are expected to build, ship, market, and run their business simultaneously — but AI tools are still siloed. A coding agent runs in one terminal; a browser agent runs somewhere in the cloud; a workflow tool connects APIs. Nobody gives you one place to manage all your CLI agents. And if you are not technical, there is a quieter frustration: watching work happen across tools you cannot directly drive.
pain.sceneDesc: Context window expired. 14 tabs open. 2 unmerged git branches. Manual copy-paste fatigue.
pain.p1Desc: You copy context from a chat window into a scratchpad, format it for a terminal, and paste the error back into the first tab. By prompt four, the model has forgotten the database schema.
pain.p2Desc: Agent loops run unchecked until your API bill spikes or a rogue patch overwrites your git staging branch without approval. You spend your evening cleaning up what was supposed to save you time.
pain.p2Metric: Zero financial guardrails in standard tools
pain.p3Desc: You are simultaneously the architect, coder, copywriter, and business analyst. Work stalls because parallel tasks collide on the same working branch.
pain.p4Title: You're not a developer — but the work still has to get done
pain.p4Desc: Software and operations need building, yet every tool seems to assume you can drive a terminal or read a diff, so the work waits on someone technical. Fabrica resolves this with plain-language direction: brief the crew like a colleague, watch progress arrive in plain language, and approve what matters before anything ships.
pain.p4Metric: Direct it in plain language — no terminal fluency required
pain.altPain: 11 PM founder desk chaos with 14 browser tabs and context fatigue

faq.headline: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.paragraph: Everything you need to know about Fabrica — the desktop platform that manages CLI agents through local terminals.

items.a1: Fabrica is a desktop platform that manages Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Devin, and other CLI agents through local terminals. Instead of raw CLI tabs, Fabrica transforms the terminal experience into a Slack-style channel interface where agents discuss approaches, delegate sub-tasks, and report progress in plain language.
items.q2: How does Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) and client-side encryption work?
items.a2: Fabrica is 100% BYOK. Your provider keys go directly to your CLI agents — never through Fabrica. Credentials are encrypted locally on your machine using AES-256 GCM in your operating system keychain. They never touch external cloud servers and are only decrypted in memory during isolated task execution.
items.q3: How do Git worktrees prevent collisions when running multiple agents?
items.a3: Git worktrees allow multiple working directories to be linked to a single repository simultaneously. When Fabrica dispatches parallel tasks, each agent runs on its own isolated branch and disk tree. Your main working branch remains pristine with zero unstaged clutter, zero merge conflicts, and zero manual stash juggling.
items.q4: How does the Mobile Companion app work?
items.a4: The Fabrica iOS and Android companion app connects to your local desktop daemon via end-to-end encrypted tunnels. You can inspect live terminal feeds, review unified diff summaries, toggle killswitches, and approve payment/deployment gates directly from your phone while away from your desk.
items.q5: Do I need to know how to code to direct Fabrica?
items.a5: No. Fabrica supports non-technical founders who want to direct work in plain language and see what happens next. You assign objectives in plain language, set budget limits, and review diffs or reports before approving. Technical leads can still use the full terminal and AST diff features.
items.q6: How much control do I have over what agents do autonomously?
items.a6: Complete control. Approval gates, hard budget caps, and risk tiers keep consequential work within your rules. You can configure Fabrica on strict step-by-step confirmation or allow continuous autonomous execution within hard financial caps and scoped directory permissions. Agents propose; you approve.
items.q7: Can agents help with business work other than writing software?
items.a7: Yes. Fabrica supports 24/7 runtime operations — customer support, ecommerce management, content pipelines, HR workflows, and business management — with the same crews directing non-coding work end to end.
items.q8: Local vs. Remote — what changes between running locally or in the cloud?
items.a8: Fabrica operates natively on your local workstation (macOS, Windows, Linux) using local git worktrees and terminal emulation. For 24/7 background routines or heavy parallel sweeps, tasks can dispatch to a headless remote VM or cloud worker over an encrypted SSH daemon tunnel.
items.a9: Spend tracking works where the CLI agent exposes quota data — currently Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. All other agents are governed by approval gates instead: high-stakes actions pause for your explicit sign-off rather than relying on cost telemetry.
